confirmed.title: The e2e global setup and db:migrate:test fall back to the dev DATABASE_URL when DATABASE_URL_TEST is unset
confirmed.scenario: A developer shell or .env has DATABASE_URL (globalpool) but no DATABASE_URL_TEST, for example an older .env or an exported variable. 'pnpm test' runs test/global-setup.ts, which spawns 'prisma.mjs migrate deploy --test-db'. Because DATABASE_URL_TEST is unset, env.mjs keeps DATABASE_URL, so pending (possibly WIP) migrations are applied to the shared dev DB. setup-env.ts:26-29 then points the tests at a hard-coded default globalpool_test that was never migrated, so the suite fails. Worse, the documented 'db:migrate:test' (package.json:21, docs/API.md:45 'reset the test database') runs 'migrate reset --force' and drops and recreates the shared dev database.
confirmed.evidence: env.mjs:13 only switches when GP_USE_TEST_DB==='1' AND DATABASE_URL_TEST is set, otherwise silently keeps DATABASE_URL. The '_test' safety regex exists only in setup-env.ts:30-31, which runs after global setup and never in the prisma wrapper.
confirmed.fix: In prisma.mjs/env.mjs, when --test-db is passed: fail if DATABASE_URL_TEST is missing (or use the same default as setup-env), and refuse any URL whose database name does not end in _test before spawning prisma.

verdicts.reason:
The defect is real, but it only fires in an environment that isn't set up that way today.

Code path confirmed:
- apps/api/scripts/prisma.mjs:10-15 turns `--test-db` into GP_USE_TEST_DB=1 and then calls loadEnvFiles().
- apps/api/scripts/env.mjs:13-15 swaps in DATABASE_URL_TEST only when it is set. Otherwise it silently keeps DATABASE_URL, the dev `globalpool` URL. There is no default and no check for a `_test` database name.
- prisma.mjs:20 then runs prisma against that URL.
- test/global-setup.ts:10-18 runs `migrate deploy --test-db` this way.
- package.json:21 `db:migrate:test` runs `migrate reset --force --test-db` the same way.

Nothing guards it earlier:
- The only `_test` regex is in test/setup-env.ts:30-31. That file is a vitest setupFile and runs after globalSetup, and the prisma wrapper never loads it.
- src/config/load-env.ts adds no check.
- setup-env.ts:26-28 falls back to a hard-coded globalpool_test URL, while env.mjs falls back to the dev DB. So the two layers can point at different databases in one run.

Result: if DATABASE_URL_TEST is missing from the shell and from both .env files, global setup migrates the dev DB while the tests use the default globalpool_test. Worse, a human running the documented `db:migrate:test` (docs/API.md:45) resets the dev database. Prisma's AI-agent consent guard would stop an agent, but not a human with --force.

Why it isn't triggered right now:
- The current global-pool/.env defines DATABASE_URL_TEST (I checked the key only, not its value).
- .env.example has had it since the first commit, and docker-compose.yml:46 sets it.
- No CI workflow exists.

So the finding's "older .env" example doesn't apply here. It takes a shell or .env that sets only DATABASE_URL. Even so, the safety switch fails open toward the shared dev DB, and the destructive script inherits that. Medium fits as a test-isolation and contamination defect.

confirmed.title: admin-a/admin-b Playwright specs reuse the shared DEMO admins at the current TOTP step: replay rejections and lockouts
confirmed.scenario: In one 'playwright test' run, admin-a.spec signs in k.osei at step S (admin-a.spec.ts:86-88), then submits an MFA code for S+1 (line 146), so totp_secrets.last_used_step = S+1. Under a minute later, admin-b.spec signs in the same k.osei with totpAt(timeStep()), which is S or S+1 (admin-b.spec.ts:97-98, 110). The API rejects it via afterTimeStep, the sign-in fails, and the test fails. Each rejected code adds to failedLoginAttempts. After ADMIN_LOGIN_MAX_ATTEMPTS=5 retries, the shared DEMO admin is locked for 15 min on the dev DB, which also blocks other agents. Other agents using the same DEMO admins cause the same rejection at random.
confirmed.evidence: _journey.ts:5-7 and :118-125 state that every step is accepted once per admin across agents, and pick max(now, last_used_step+1) from the DB. admin-a/admin-b signIn() ignores last_used_step. totp.service.ts:165-173 rejects any step <= lastUsedStep, and admin-auth.service.ts:84-93 counts it as a failed login.
confirmed.fix: Reuse the _journey freshCode/adminCode helper (read last_used_step, wait for the next unused step) in admin-a.spec and admin-b.spec. Or give each spec its own seeded admin instead of the shared DEMO admins.

verdicts.reason:
I confirmed this in the code. apps/web/package.json runs test:e2e as a bare `playwright test`. playwright.config.ts uses testDir ./e2e with workers:1 and fullyParallel:false, so files run in path order and admin-b.spec.ts starts right after admin-a.spec.ts. In admin-a.spec.ts, signIn() logs k.osei in with step S (lines 87-88). Line 146 then submits totpAt(osei, S+1). That goes through admin-security.service.ts:38 into totp.verifyActive, and the success assertion at line 149 shows it was accepted, so last_used_step for k.osei becomes S+1 (totp.service.ts:170-176). admin-b.spec.ts:97-98 then signs in the same k.osei with timeStep(). The login UI auto-submits on the sixth digit (login.tsx:494). In otplib 13.6.0, verify skips every counter at or below afterTimeStep (`k(e,c)` returns e<=c), so step S or S+1 cannot match. verifyRow returns ok:false and bumps failedAttempts, and admin-auth.service.ts:84-95 counts a failed admin login. The expectation at admin-b.spec.ts:99 then times out.

The window is real. admin-b only works if its sign-in falls in step S+2 or later, which needs 30 to 60 s to pass after admin-a's osei login, depending on where in step S that login happened. The rest of admin-a (osei's remaining steps, Iyer's sign-in and approval, user and audit pages, plus the short unauthenticated test) plausibly finishes inside that window once pages are compiled. So the failure is flaky or frequent rather than theoretical. Neither spec reads last_used_step. _journey.ts:4-7 and :118-125 already document this exact cross-agent replay problem and handle it, which confirms the hazard is known.

One part is overstated. A successful login resets failedLoginAttempts (admin-auth.service.ts:110-113), so the 15-minute lockout needs 5 failed sign-ins in a row with no success between them. That only happens with repeated reruns or other agents colliding. It does not follow from a single run. The flaky-test and contamination failure itself is real, and medium severity fits.

confirmed.title: player.e2e and openapi.e2e leave an open under_review withdrawal behind on every run
confirmed.scenario: Each run of player.e2e (100.00 under_review, flagged, line 317) and openapi.e2e (50.00, openapi.e2e-spec.ts:131) leaves a withdrawal open forever in globalpool_test. The admin queue (oldest first) grows by 2+ per run. This is the root cause of the admin.e2e 'flagged withdrawals need FOUR EYES' failure once more than 20 were open. That test now works around it by reading the first and last page (admin.e2e-spec.ts:231-250), but the leak keeps going, and the queue SLA/summary aggregates in admin-ops and any future first-page assertion drift with test history.
confirmed.evidence: wallet.e2e-spec.ts:291-292 already cancels its withdrawal with the comment 'Leave no open review behind in the shared test database'. player and openapi do not. A read-only count in globalpool_test shows 51 under_review withdrawals (21 created in the 05:00 hour alone).
confirmed.fix: POST /withdrawals/:id/cancel at the end of both tests (or in afterAll), as wallet.e2e does.

verdicts.reason:
The finding holds up. I couldn't refute it. In apps/api/test/player.e2e-spec.ts (lines 313-352) the test creates a 100.00 withdrawal and asserts status under_review, flagged=true and requiresFourEyes=true, then ends without cancelling it. Its afterAll (line 24) only calls t.close(). apps/api/test/openapi.e2e-spec.ts (lines 126-145) creates a 50.00 withdrawal to the new address 0x5555… and never cancels it either. Its afterAll (line 41) also only closes the app. That withdrawal also lands in under_review: in MockAmlProvider (src/modules/aml/aml.provider.ts:82-86), a new destination gives decision 'review', and withdrawals.service.ts:327 maps that to under_review.

Nothing else cleans these up. global-setup.ts runs only `migrate deploy` and says no reset is needed. setup-env.ts sets JOBS_ENABLED=false. I found no code that sweeps or expires under_review withdrawals.

wallet.e2e-spec.ts:291-292 shows the intended pattern: it cancels its withdrawal with the comment "Leave no open review behind". admin.e2e-spec.ts:231-250 already works around the growing oldest-first queue by reading both the first and the last page.

A read-only count in globalpool_test now shows 53 under_review withdrawals, up from the 51 cited, so the leak is still growing. Other files (admin-console, chain) may leak too, but that doesn't weaken this finding. The impact is limited to test-DB contamination and drifting queue aggregates, so low severity is right.

confirmed.title: sanitizeAmount reads ',' as a decimal point, and a unit test locks that in, so pasted amounts lose their thousands
confirmed.scenario: The app shows amounts with comma thousands separators (Amount renders '9,215.30'; the AmountInput header shows 'Available 9,215.30 USDT'). A player pastes 9,215.30 into the withdraw amount and gets 9.21. Typing '1,000' as a deposit or participation limit in limit-setter.tsx:143/279 gives 1.00. The deposit-flow amount (deposit-flow.tsx:647/787) does the same.
confirmed.evidence: raw.replace(/,/g,'.') runs before the dot split, so '1,234.50' becomes '1.234.50' and then '1.23'. apps/web/test/logic.test.ts:13 asserts sanitizeAmount('1,234.5', 2) === '1.23', so the test enshrines the wrong result instead of catching it.
confirmed.fix: Strip ',' when the string also contains '.', or when ',' is followed by exactly 3 digits (thousands grouping). Only treat a lone ',' as a decimal point. Update logic.test.ts to expect '1234.50'.

verdicts.reason:
The finding holds. In apps/web/src/components/domain/amount-input.tsx:35, sanitizeAmount runs raw.replace(/,/g,'.') before it splits on '.'. So '9,215.30' becomes '9.215.30' and then '9.21', and '1,000' becomes '1.00'.

The app itself shows comma as the thousands separator. formatUSDT in packages/shared/src/money.ts:235 uses groupThousands with a '.' decimal, and AmountInput's own header renders 'Available 9,215.30 USDT'.

All the paths in the finding are reachable:
- AmountInput onChange (line 93), used by withdraw-flow.tsx:696.
- deposit-flow.tsx:647 and 787.
- limit-setter.tsx:279 on change, and again at submit at line 143.

Nothing upstream normalizes the value first. These inputs are plain text with inputMode='decimal', so the browser does no locale parsing.

apps/web/test/logic.test.ts:13 asserts sanitizeAmount('1,234.5', 2) === '1.23', which locks in the wrong result. The docstring ('1,5' → '1.5') shows that treating a comma as a decimal point was intended, but that clashes with the app's own display format for any value with grouped thousands.

It stays low severity because the inputs are controlled, so the player sees the mangled value in the field before submitting. Server-side checks still apply.

confirmed.title: CI never uses the Foundry 'ci' profile, so contracts get 1,024 fuzz runs and 64 invariant runs instead of 10,000 and 512
confirmed.scenario: foundry.toml defines [profile.ci.fuzz] runs=10_000 and [profile.ci.invariant] runs=512. The workflow's env block has no FOUNDRY_PROFILE, and the @gp/contracts test script runs a plain 'forge test'. So CI runs the default profile (fuzz 1,024, invariant 64x256), and the stronger CI fuzzing of the draw/settlement invariants never runs anywhere.
confirmed.evidence: grep finds no FOUNDRY_PROFILE in .github/workflows/global-pool-ci.yml or packages/contracts/package.json. The test step is 'pnpm -r test', which runs 'sh scripts/forge.sh test'.
confirmed.fix: Set FOUNDRY_PROFILE: ci in the workflow env (or on the Test step), or add a 'test:ci' script that passes --profile ci and call it from CI.

verdicts.reason:
The finding is real. CI never selects the ci profile, so the stronger fuzz and invariant settings never run there.

1. packages/contracts/foundry.toml sets the default profile to fuzz runs=1024 (lines 21-23) and invariant runs=64, depth=256 (lines 25-28). The ci profile raises fuzz runs to 10_000 (lines 30-31) and invariant runs to 512, depth=128 (lines 33-35).
2. /home/user/Claude/.github/workflows/global-pool-ci.yml is the only workflow in the repo. Its env block (lines 56-81) has no FOUNDRY_PROFILE. Its Test step (lines 117-118) runs a plain `pnpm -r test`, with no profile flag.
3. In packages/contracts/package.json the `test` script is `sh scripts/forge.sh test && node --test ...`. scripts/forge.sh just runs `exec forge "$@"`, so no `--profile` or FOUNDRY_PROFILE is added on the way.
4. Forge does not switch to the ci profile because CI=true is set. It only reads FOUNDRY_PROFILE, which nothing sets.
5. A repo-wide grep finds no FOUNDRY_PROFILE or `--profile ci` anywhere outside the contracts README. The README (line 76) says `FOUNDRY_PROFILE=ci` gives 10,000 runs and 512 x 128 invariants, so the ci profile was clearly meant to be used.
6. No test file has a `forge-config` inline override that would raise the run counts.

So CI runs the draw/settlement fuzz and invariant suites at 1,024 and 64 x 256. Low severity fits: this is test strength, not a runtime defect.
